sheet-2.description: Sheet 2 covers the western end of downtown Summit, from De Forest Avenue at the top to Park Avenue at the bottom, and from Kent Place Boulevard and Chestnut Avenue on the west to Highland Avenue and Maple on the east. Springfield Avenue crosses the middle of the sheet from the lower left towards the upper right, a business street of two and three storey stores, drugstores and a bank on its north side between Woodland Avenue and Highland Avenue, where the brick and frame stores stand shoulder to shoulder. North of Springfield Avenue stand the M.E. Church of Summit with its parish house, the Strand Theatre with a laundry beside it, and a scatter of frame dwellings along De Forest Avenue and Woodland Avenue; a large block numbered 99 east of Woodland Avenue holds dwellings, a carpenter and a painter. The Delaware, Lackawanna & Western Railroad crosses the sheet diagonally from the left edge to the lower right, with Railroad Avenue running along its south side. South of the tracks are warehouses and shops, among them the Summit Fireproof Warehouse Co. Inc., an iron works storage building and several auto repair shops, with frame houses on Chestnut Avenue. The American Apron Co. stands on the north side of the tracks beside Maple. Park Avenue and Cedar Street at the foot of the sheet bound largely vacant blocks belonging to sheets 17 and 23. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch; neighbouring sheet numbers 17, 18, 19, 23 and 3 are printed in the margins.
notes: De Forest Avenue is Deforest Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Park Avenue is Broad Street in OpenStreetMap.
Highland Avenue north of Springfield Avenue and Maple south of it are both Maple Street in OpenStreetMap.
The hand-picked point at Maple Street and Springfield Avenue lies on the Highland Avenue water pipe line at the street centre; the detector paired the building face instead.
Downtown streets here fit with residuals of 3 to 5 m (Park Avenue junctions).
Downtown, 50 ft. Springfield Av, Woodland Av, Maple/Highland Av, Park Av (= Broad St), railroad. Maple/Springfield hand-picked.

sheet-3.description: Sheet 3 shows the commercial centre of Summit around the junction of Springfield Avenue and Beechwood Road, bounded by De Forest Avenue at the top, Highland Avenue on the west, Summit Avenue on the east and the Delaware, Lackawanna & Western Railroad at the bottom. Springfield Avenue crosses the sheet from left to right, lined on both sides by two and three storey brick stores with their street numbers. The north-west block (100) holds the Lincoln Public School, a fireproof concrete building, above a row of shops and a bank. North-east of Beechwood Road stand St. John's Lutheran Church, an undertaker and a few stone-trimmed dwellings, with printing works and shops below. South of Springfield Avenue the Bassett Building, the Central Building, the Post Office, an electric storage building and a long row of lodge rooms and shops fill the block between Maple and Beechwood Road; to the east are a large vacant tile building, the Municipal Building and the Fire Department, and a further block of auto repair and sales premises between Bank and Union Place. Franklin Place runs below Union Place to Summit Avenue. At the foot of the sheet the railroad passes the Summit depot, which has platforms and a pedestrian bridge, with a switch house to the east; the two blocks south of Railroad Avenue are lettered Park. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch; neighbouring sheets 2, 4, 19, 20 and 23 are named in the margins.
notes: De Forest Avenue is Deforest Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Park Avenue is Broad Street in OpenStreetMap.
Highland Avenue north of Springfield Avenue and Maple south of it are both Maple Street in OpenStreetMap.
Bank is Bank Street in OpenStreetMap.
Elm is Elm Street in OpenStreetMap.
Downtown, 50 ft. Springfield Av, Beechwood Rd, Summit Av, Bank, Union Pl, depot.

sheet-4.description: Sheet 4 lies east of the Summit business centre and shows the stretch of Springfield Avenue from Summit Avenue eastward, the residential streets north and south of it, and the railroad yard at the foot of the sheet. At the upper left a row of stores, an office building and auto repairing premises line the east side of Summit Avenue between Springfield Avenue and Franklin Place, including a fire department building and a printing works. East of Glenwood Place the blocks turn to housing: between Glenwood Place, Irving Place and Springfield Avenue stand frame dwellings, with a store and a long blue-coloured building at the Springfield Avenue corner, and further east blocks 108 and 109 contain two-storey frame houses on narrow lots, with the First Church of Christ, Scientist on Rutheven Place. South of Franklin Place the lots are lined with frame dwellings backing on the Delaware, Lackawanna & Western Railroad, whose many tracks cross the lower part of the sheet; a turntable, a small circular park with a fountain and the end of Summit Avenue lie at the lower left. West of the tracks near Franklin Place there are auto sales and service shops, a plumber and a garage for ten cars, and a dress factory near Summit Avenue. Sheet 3 adjoins on the west, sheet 5 below, and sheets 20 and 25 above and to the right. The sheet is drawn at 50 feet to an inch.
notes: Rutheven Place is Ruthven Place in OpenStreetMap.
Glenwood Place is printed Glenwood on the sheet and Glenwood Place in OpenStreetMap.
Park Avenue is Broad Street in OpenStreetMap.
The drawn Morristown Line railroad measured about 13 m from its modern line along the track; rail crossings were not used as control.
Downtown east, 50 ft. Springfield Av, Glenwood/Irving/Waldron/Rutheven, Franklin Pl, yards. Drawn Morristown Line about 13 m from the modern line.

sheet-5.description: Sheet 5 covers the south-eastern edge of downtown Summit, below the railroad, between Summit Avenue on the west and Sylvan Road on the east. The upper part of the sheet shows the Delaware, Lackawanna & Western Railroad yard, with a turntable and water tank at the left, many parallel tracks and, at the right, the D.L. & W. freight house, which fills a long block above Park Avenue. Park Avenue crosses the sheet below the yard, and the two blocks south of it are industrial: a row of auto sales and service garages with gas tanks along the avenue, then Corby's Enterprise Laundry Co., the Summit Cement Block Co., an oil storage building, the Sweet-Kleen Laundry Inc. and a sheet metal works, with the Central Atlantic States Service Corporation's ice manufacturing and storage plant to the east. Below them the sheet changes to residential streets laid out at a slant: Walnut, Sylvan Terrace and Beauvoir Avenue run from the south-west towards the north-east, lined with frame dwellings on narrow lots, many with garages. Beauvoir Place drops from Walnut to a pipe junction at its south end, and Sylvan Road curves down the right side, marked not opened below the houses. The part is drawn at 50 feet to an inch and is turned by roughly 16 degrees from north-up, its compass pointing up and to the left; the neighbouring sheets 4, 23 and 24 are named in the margins.
notes: Park Avenue is Broad Street in OpenStreetMap.
Walnut is Walnut Street in OpenStreetMap.
North points up and to the left on this part (fit rotation -16 degrees).
The Summit Avenue and Walnut junction was not used: a hand-picked point on the water pipe centre lines disagreed with the other control by about 5 m.
Sylvan Road below Sylvan Terrace is marked not opened.
Park Av/Walnut district, 50 ft, turned about -16 degrees. Few junctions; one hand pick.

sheet-6-1.description: The main part of Sheet 6 shows the northern tip of Summit where it meets the Borough of Chatham at the Passaic River. River Road crosses the lower half of the part from south-west to north-east, with Plain Street, Chatham Road, Lewis Avenue and Greenfield Avenue leaving it to the north; Chatham Road runs north to a bridge over the river into Chatham. The Passaic River and the city line wind around the top and right of the part, with a small island in the river and a steel railroad bridge crossing it. Development is sparse: a few frame dwellings and garages along River Road and Chatham Road, and large open lots. Three works are drawn in detail: the Jersey Central Power and Light Company's Summit sub-station beside Chatham Road near the river, the City of Summit sewage pumping station east of Chatham Road, and the Columbia Cleaning and Dyeing Company's plant on Chatham Road with its watchman and clock and steam heat noted. A fireproof structure stands in the large lot numbered 17 between Chatham Road and Greenfield Avenue. A heavy line across the lower part of the sheet separates this part from a second part drawn turned on the same page, and the land south of River Road is marked as covered by the map of Chatham. The part is drawn at 100 feet to an inch, with north pointing up and to the right.
notes: Margin notes read "See Map of Chatham" along the river and south of River Road.
Placed from four junctions along River Road only (helmert); low confidence away from River Road.

100 ft, two parts. Part 1: River Rd at Chatham Rd by the Passaic (helmert on River Rd junctions). Part 2: River Rd east of Woodland Av drawn turned (north about 66 deg), anchored on one hand-picked junction.

sheet-6-2.description: The second part of Sheet 6, below the heavy dividing line, is drawn turned so that north points to the upper right. It shows River Road where it runs north-east along the south bank of the Passaic River, from Woodland Avenue past Iris Road to the Morris and Essex Turnpike at the right edge, which forms the city line there. The river with its city line runs across the upper half of the part, a branch of it reaching up towards the top, and the land beyond is the Borough of Chatham, covered by the map of Chatham. A brook crosses River Road towards the river. Buildings are few: a police house on River Road near Iris Road, a small farm group of poultry houses, a silo, a milk house and sheds in the lot numbered 15, and a large frame dwelling with a pump house beside the turnpike. Much of the area between River Road and the river is open. The part is drawn at 100 feet to an inch.
notes: Morris and Essex Turnpike at this point is no longer a through road; River Road east of Iris Road was rebuilt for the John F. Kennedy Parkway (Route 24) interchange.

Placed from one hand-picked junction (River Road / Woodland Avenue) at the atlas scale with north set to 66 degrees from River Road's direction; Iris Road is drawn about 9 m farther from Woodland Avenue than today's junction, so it was left out. Low confidence.

100 ft, two parts. Part 1: River Rd at Chatham Rd by the Passaic (helmert on River Rd junctions). Part 2: River Rd east of Woodland Av drawn turned (north about 66 deg), anchored on one hand-picked junction.

sheet-7.description: Sheet 7 covers the north-west corner of Summit along the Chatham border, where the sheet is turned so that north points to the upper left. River Road runs down the left side from the top corner past Chatham Road to Morris Avenue and then south-west to the Passaic River bridge at Passaic Avenue. The top of the sheet is a strip of house lots between Greenfield Avenue, marked not open, and Lewis Avenue, mostly small frame dwellings with garages. A second row of lots lies along Lewis Avenue below it, and further down the blocks on both sides of Plain, which meets River Road, and Morris Avenue are thinly built, with a large part of block 24 left blank. East of Plain, Aubrey runs south from Lewis Avenue to Morris Avenue and carries a dense line of houses. Lafayette Avenue crosses the right edge of the sheet and bends south-west below Morris Avenue, where the blocks around Lincoln Avenue and Madison Avenue hold a small commercial group, the Neighborhood House with a kindergarten,. In the lower middle a large lot is occupied by the greenhouses of Chas. H. Hagert, owner, leased to Colle Bros, with potting houses and a stable. The Passaic River and the municipal boundary line with Chatham run down the lower left, crossed by a bridge, and a margin note refers to the map of Chatham. Water pipes of four to eight inches are drawn in the main streets. The south-east corner is blank and numbered for the neighbouring sheets 35 and 8. The scale is 100 feet to an inch.
notes: Aubrey is Aubrey Street and Plain is Plain Street in OpenStreetMap.
Sheridan Avenue, drawn at the right edge, is not in OpenStreetMap.
Greenfield Avenue is marked not open on the sheet; Lafayette Avenue is marked not open north of Sheridan Avenue.
The margin note 'See Map of Chatham' refers to the adjoining Chatham map west of the Passaic River.
100 ft, turned (rotation about -53). River Road / Chatham border, Morris Av.

sheet-8.description: Sheet 8 covers the area around the Morris Avenue approach to Summit's north-west boundary, drawn with north pointing to the upper left. Morris runs diagonally up the sheet from Lafayette Avenue at the left edge to Bedford Road at the top right. Lafayette Avenue carries a row of small frame dwellings on its east side and the Washington Public School and the Union Broad Silk Company works stand at its junction with Morris. Further along Morris, between Beverly Road and Gates Avenue, is the brick silk mill of the Shanazarian company, and beyond Gates Avenue the large brick factory of E. Gerli and Company, a tenant factory building with sprinklers, its own water system and watchman's clock. Gates Avenue runs south-east from Morris with houses and a few small lots, and Weaver runs south from the Morris frontage past a row of two-storey dwellings to a group of tenements. At the far right Larger and Hurrell's greenhouses are drawn as long yellow ranges. The upper left is a large vacant tract, block 307, bounded by Sheridan Avenue, marked not open, and Lafayette Avenue, with a Proposed Street drawn across it. The lower half is mostly blank or sparsely built: Madison Avenue crosses the bottom from Lafayette Avenue, Evergreen Place leaves it at the south, and Kent Place Boulevard curves in at the lower right beside a few scattered houses marked from plans. Water pipes of four and six inches are shown in the main streets, with hydrants and telephone and fire-alarm boxes. The sheet is drawn at 100 feet to an inch.
notes: Evergreen Place is Evergreen Road in OpenStreetMap; Morris is Morris Avenue, Weaver is Weaver Street.
Sheridan Avenue is not in OpenStreetMap at this location (Sheridan Road lies elsewhere); a Proposed Street is lettered across block 307.
The Union Broad Silk Company and the neighbouring silk mill lettering was not read in full; the E. Gerli and Company factory and Larger and Hurrell greenhouses are named on the sheet.
Lowell, Webster and Montrose Avenues exist today across the blank lower-left area but are not drawn.
100 ft, turned (rotation about -61). Morris Avenue silk mills, Beverly Rd, Bedford Rd.

sheet-9.description: Sheet 9 covers a strip of south-western Summit between Kent Place Boulevard along the top and Beekman Road along the bottom, with Passaic Avenue running down the left edge. It is drawn with north up at 100 feet to an inch. The upper third holds two narrow bands of large lots, one facing Kent Place Boulevard and one facing West End Avenue, separated by the abandoned right of way of the D.L. and W. Railroad, which curves across the sheet under block 51. Both bands are thinly built, with a few frame dwellings, outbuildings and a stable scattered across deep lots, and a larger house in grounds at the upper right. Below West End Avenue a wide unbuilt tract runs down to the double-track Delaware, Lackawanna and Western main line, which crosses the sheet from the left bridge over Passaic Avenue to the right edge. A second line of the same railroad, noted as the Passaic and Delaware Branch, rises from the lower left and crosses the middle of block 52, with a triangular lot between the tracks and Passaic Avenue. The lower right is a row of frame houses and a small group of other buildings along the north side of Beekman Road, with a water pipe and telephone box, and Beekman Terrace enters Beekman Road twice, at the lower middle and near the right, as a narrow street. Risk Avenue leaves Passaic Avenue at the lower left. Water pipes of four and six inches are drawn in Kent Place Boulevard, Passaic Avenue and Beekman Road. Blocks 14, 15, 10 and 35 mark the neighbouring sheets.
notes: The D.L. & W.R.R. is lettered as an abandoned right of way north of West End Avenue; the main line and a branch are drawn south of it (OpenStreetMap: Morristown Line and Gladstone Branch).

Control is thin: only four junctions were detected, two on Passaic Avenue (drawn narrower than the modern right of way) and two at Beekman Terrace; Beekman Road / Passaic Avenue lies at the left edge of the scan and was not usable.
Risk Avenue is not placed in OpenStreetMap at this junction; Constantine Place and Risk Avenue lie just west of Passaic Avenue.

sheet-10-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 10 is the main map, a district of south-western Summit between Kent Place Boulevard and Springfield Avenue, drawn with north up at 100 feet to an inch. Kent Place Boulevard runs along the top edge and then sweeps south-east in a long curve to the right edge, with a row of small frame dwellings and outbuildings on its inner side and larger houses in grounds, one with a blue-coloured roof, further along. A strip of lots with a few houses lies between West End Avenue and the abandoned D.L. and W. right of way at the upper left. Across the middle the double-track main line of the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad runs from left to right, joined from the lower left by the Passaic and Delaware Branch, which fans out into several tracks. South of the railroad the blocks of large lots are bounded by Beekman Road, which crosses the sheet from the lower left to High at the right, and carry scattered houses, a stable and a pink-coloured brick building. Oakley Avenue and Fairview Avenue are short streets running south from Beekman Road, Fairview being the longer. The lower right quarter is a large partly built tract, block 88, with a greenhouse, a larger frame house and scattered dwellings, and High runs down the right edge to a junction with New England Avenue and then to Springfield Avenue, which crosses the bottom right corner. Water pipes of four to eight inches are drawn in most streets. A boxed second part of the sheet occupies the lower left corner, and a dash-dot line marked A and B along the bottom of this part joins it to the inset. The compass is drawn above the inset.
notes: High is High Street in OpenStreetMap.
The railroad lettered D.L. & W. R.R. (P & D Branch) is the Gladstone Branch and Morristown Line in OpenStreetMap.
Kent Place Boulevard / Madison Avenue lies at the top edge and was hand-picked; only four other junctions were detected, so control is thin.
100 ft, two parts: main (Kent Place Blvd, Beekman Rd, High) and a boxed lower-left continuation (Fairview Av / Springfield Av), anchored on one junction.

sheet-10-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 10 is a boxed section in the lower left corner, outlined by a heavy line, that continues the main map southward beyond a dash-dot line lettered A and B. It is drawn at the same scale and direction as the main part, with north up at 100 feet to an inch. Fairview Avenue runs south along the left side of the box between its two boundary lines, with a six-inch water pipe, and meets Springfield Avenue at the bottom left corner. Springfield Avenue crosses the box diagonally to the upper right, with a four-inch pipe and a hydrant, and Pine Grove Avenue branches from it at the bottom. The area between Fairview Avenue and Springfield Avenue is part of block 88, mostly open land with a pair of small frame houses near the A line and a single dwelling at the top. Blocks 15 and 16 are numbered on the other side of the streets, and block 10 is the sheet number. The scale bar of the sheet is printed at the foot of the box.
notes: Pine Grove Avenue is Pinegrove Avenue in OpenStreetMap.

Only one junction (Fairview Avenue / Springfield Avenue) is used; the part is anchored on it with the scale and direction of part 1, so it is low confidence. Pinegrove Avenue / Springfield Avenue was left out because the narrow Springfield Avenue was measured about 5 m from its modern right-of-way centre.
