sheet-11.description: Sheet 11 covers the Kent Place Boulevard and Morris Avenue district of south-western Summit, drawn at 100 feet to an inch with north turned about 20 degrees clockwise from the top of the page. Kent Place Boulevard enters from the upper left, where High branches off to the south-west, and runs diagonally to the right edge past a continuous row of frame dwellings, with the double-track main line of the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad running beside it across the middle of the sheet. Morris Avenue runs down the right side. At the upper right a pair of short streets, Edgar (Kent Place North) and Kent Place (South), serve rows of small two-and-a-half storey dwellings on block 309. The upper left is mostly open land with a few large houses, a pink-coloured works lettered as a tenant factory with electric power and fire pails, and the Kent Place frontage of block 54. South of the railroad block 92 and block 93 form long lots between High and New England Avenue, which curves south from High to Springfield Avenue and carries the larger houses of the sheet. Near the lower right stand the Dominican Convent with its chapel, the Rosary Shrine Roman Catholic church, and the First Baptist Church, all marked as heated and lighted. Springfield Avenue, George Street and Blackburn Road run along the bottom edge. Beekman Road enters from the left at High with a four-inch water pipe, and water pipes of four to eight inches and hydrants are shown in most streets.
notes: High is High Street in OpenStreetMap, which no longer joins Kent Place Boulevard where the sheet draws it: the modern node lies about 59 m south-east of the drawn junction, so that junction was left out.
Edgar Street / Morris Avenue is the junction of the street lettered Edgar (Kent Place North) with Morris Avenue.
Junctions on Springfield Avenue at the bottom edge (Blackburn Road, George Street, Morris Avenue) and Morris Avenue / Norwood Avenue at the right edge were not detected and are not used.
100 ft, rotation about +27. Kent Place Blvd, New England Av, Morris Av. High St / Kent Place Blvd realigned (59 m), left out.

sheet-12.description: Sheet 12 covers the north-west edge of Summit, an area of large estates and unbuilt tracts between Morris Avenue on the west and Woodland Avenue on the east. Beverly Road crosses the top of the sheet, bending from the north-west corner towards Woodland Avenue, and Norwood Avenue curves across the bottom left. The north half is mostly open land divided into large lots, with only a few scattered frame dwellings; the sheet number 35 marks a neighbouring sheet beyond it. The Oratory School for Boys stands west of Canoe Brook Parkway on Morris Avenue, drawn as a class room and dormitory building and a dining room and kitchen building, with steam heat and electric light and no fire apparatus. Bedford Road and Nuthurst Road run east and north-east between Morris Avenue and Woodland Avenue, with large houses and outbuildings on long lots. The lower right corner is the most built-up part: Margaretta Court, Sherman Avenue and Mac Gregor Road bound a block of narrow lots with frame dwellings, garages and a few brick and vacant buildings, close to Woodland Avenue. A tracing of an unopened street, labelled Not Opened, runs near the top edge and a proposed street joins Beverly Road at the upper left. Water pipes of four and six inches with hydrants are drawn in the streets. The sheet is drawn at 100 feet to an inch, and its north arrow points about 20 degrees right of the top of the page.
notes: Nuthurst Road, Margaretta Court and Sheridan Avenue are not in OpenStreetMap; Mac Gregor Road is McGregor Road there.
Proposed Street is marked Proposed and a street near the top edge is marked Not Opened.
Oratory School for Boys stands on Morris Avenue north of Bedford Road.
Canoe Brook Parkway is drawn ending short of Beverly Road.
100 ft, rotation about +31. Oratory School for Boys, Bedford and Nuthurst roads.

sheet-13.description: Sheet 13 covers a residential district in the north-west of Summit, drawn with north towards the left of the page. Summit Avenue crosses the top edge, and Hillcrest Avenue runs down the left side, curving east at the bottom to meet Woodland Avenue. Badeau Avenue bounds the right side from Summit Avenue down to Bellevue Avenue and Beechwood Road, and Woodland Avenue crosses the lower part of the sheet. Between them the blocks are cut by Edgemont Avenue, Bellevue Avenue, Beechwood Road and Llwellyn Road, with Lyric Lane, marked as impassable in July 1929, running down the middle. The houses are mostly detached frame dwellings with garages on large lots, with a few of stone and a few brick and vacant buildings. Larger houses with outbuildings stand along Hillcrest Avenue and Beechwood Road, and a small group stands near Edgemont Avenue and Badeau Avenue. Much of the ground between the streets is still open, laid out in lots that run back from the street lines but not yet built on. The lower left corner shows only a few buildings among unbuilt lots near Woodland Avenue, Bedford Road and Beverly Road. Four-inch and six-inch water pipes with hydrants are drawn in the streets and the widths of several streets are marked, 40 and 50 feet. The adjoining sheets are numbered in the margins as 37, 36, 19 and 12. The sheet is drawn at 100 feet to an inch.
notes: Lyric Lane is marked Impassable July 1929 and is not in OpenStreetMap.
Llwellyn Road is Llewelyn Road in OpenStreetMap; the printed spelling is hard to read.
Nuthurst Road is not in OpenStreetMap.
100 ft, turned (north to the left, rotation -77). Hillcrest/Badeau/Beechwood district; Lyric Lane impassable in July 1929.

sheet-14.description: Sheet 14 covers a thinly built residential and semi-rural district on the western side of Summit, along the city line. Springfield Avenue crosses the upper half of the sheet from the left edge to the right, where it is joined by Passaic Avenue running up from the junction near the top left. Beekman Road runs along the top, with Beekman Terrace branching south-east from it near the right edge. Division Avenue runs down the left side from top to bottom and carries a dash-dot line that marks the city line. Two brooks cross the sheet from left to right, one below Springfield Avenue and a second, larger one below it that is bridged or culverted where it meets Division Avenue. West of Division Avenue, Lavina Court curves through a small subdivision of narrow lots with a few frame dwellings. South of the brook Sunset Drive leaves Division Avenue and sweeps east and then south along the right edge, and Valley View Avenue runs along the bottom of the sheet. Almost all buildings are two-storey frame dwellings with small outbuildings on large or long narrow lots, and much of the east is open land. A group of long blue glass-house or greenhouse buildings marked J. N. Anderson stands beside Passaic Avenue, and a few buildings are brick or tile. Six-inch and eight-inch water pipes with hydrants are drawn in the main streets. The sheet is drawn at 100 feet to an inch; the adjoining sheets are numbered 35, 80, 15, 81, 82 and 34 on its margins, and 335, 336 and 79 appear to the west across the city line.
notes: Passaic Avenue / Springfield Avenue is today the junction of Passaic Avenue, Springfield Avenue and Old Springfield Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
A dash-dot city line runs along Division Avenue.
Valley View Avenue is lettered 'VALLEY VIEW AV.' and continues off the sheet at the right.
100 ft, rotation about +17. Springfield Av, Passaic Av, Beekman Rd, Division Av, Sunset Dr.

sheet-15-1.description: The main part of Sheet 15 covers a residential and nursery district on the west side of Summit, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. Beekman Road crosses the top left corner, with Beekman Terrace looping south from it past a row of small frame dwellings. Oakley Avenue and Fairview Avenue run down from the top to Springfield Avenue, which crosses the middle of the part from west to east; their narrow lots are lined with two-storey frame dwellings, while the land west of Oakley Avenue is divided into large lots with scattered houses. South of Springfield Avenue a brook crosses the part from west to east. The lower half is dominated by greenhouses: the Edith A. Kerr greenhouses on the left and the large range of the Harry O. May greenhouses, with boiler house, office and storage, on the right, built of frame on concrete bases. Sunset Drive comes down the left side to Valley View Avenue, which with Blackburn Road forms the bottom edge, and the Summit Tennis Club is marked near Sunset Drive. Pine Grove Avenue runs down the right edge with Prospect Street and Blackburn Place leaving it. A heavy line at the upper right cuts off a second part of the sheet showing Beekman Road drawn turned.
notes: Pine Grove Avenue is Pinegrove Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
Greenhouses of Harry O. May and of Edith A. Kerr; Summit Tennis Club near Sunset Drive.
100 ft, two parts. Part 1 main map (Beekman Rd to Valley View Av, greenhouses). Part 2 top right: Beekman Rd at Fairview and Oakley Avs, drawn turned (north about -64 deg), helmert on two junctions.

sheet-15-2.description: The second part of Sheet 15, enclosed by a heavy line at the upper right of the page, shows a short stretch of Beekman Road with the ends of Fairview Avenue and Oakley Avenue, the part of the district beyond the top edge of the main map. It is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the upper left, as its own north arrow shows. Beekman Road runs down the left side, Fairview Avenue leaves it at the top and Oakley Avenue lower down, both fifty feet wide with six-inch water pipes, and the large block between them is numbered 87. A dash-dot match line marked A crosses the part diagonally. No buildings are drawn in this part; the July 1929 Summit title cartouche sits in the block.
notes: Placed from two junctions (Beekman Road at Fairview Avenue and at Oakley Avenue) with a helmert fit; low confidence.
100 ft, two parts. Part 1 main map (Beekman Rd to Valley View Av, greenhouses). Part 2 top right: Beekman Rd at Fairview and Oakley Avs, drawn turned (north about -64 deg), helmert on two junctions.

sheet-16.description: Sheet 16 covers a residential district in the south-west of Summit between Springfield Avenue and Ashland Place. Springfield Avenue crosses the top of the sheet diagonally, with a stream running into it from the left, and the block next to it holds a strip of small shops and dwellings between Blackburn Road and High, with a brook crossing the lots behind. High runs south from Springfield Avenue to Prospect, Blackburn Road runs down the right side as a long straight street before turning to curve south-west, and Pine Grove Avenue forms the left boundary. Prospect crosses the middle of the sheet from left to right and Blackburn Place runs parallel to it below. Brook Court is a short street between Blackburn Road and the lots behind Springfield Avenue. The streets have mostly two-storey frame dwellings with outbuildings, and the middle of the sheet, between Springfield Avenue and Prospect, is largely open land with a few larger houses. A greenhouse or glass shed stands beside High. The Oak Knoll School of the Holy Child occupies a large lot beside the curve of Blackburn Road at the lower right, and the south-west corner holds Oak Knoll Drive, a short street whose lots are marked as laid out from plans. Larned Road forms the right edge, with Oakland Place and Linden Place and Ashland Place leaving it. Water pipes of four to six inches are drawn in most streets. The sheet is drawn at 100 feet to an inch; neighbouring sheet numbers 10, 11, 17, 22, 21, 34 and 15 are printed in the margins.
notes: Pine Grove Avenue is Pinegrove Avenue in OpenStreetMap; Prospect is Prospect Street and High is High Street; Ashland Place is Ashland Road.
Oak Knoll Drive is not in OpenStreetMap.
Oak Knoll School of the Holy Child stands beside the curve of Blackburn Road.
100 ft. Springfield Av, Prospect, Blackburn Rd/Pl, Pine Grove Av, Larned Rd, Oak Knoll School.

sheet-17.description: Sheet 17 covers the area on the south-west side of Summit's business centre, from Springfield Avenue and Park Avenue at the top to Linden Place at the bottom, and from Blackburn Road and Larned Road on the left to Maple on the right. Springfield Avenue crosses the top left and meets New England Avenue and Tulip near the Hotel Suburban, a large brick and tile hotel with its fire-protection equipment described beside it. Locust Drive runs diagonally from there to Morris Avenue, past the blocks bounded by George and Manley; the diagonal street beyond it is lettered Locust Drive and, in brackets, Park Avenue West, and Park Avenue runs along the top right. Morris Avenue runs from the upper centre to the right edge, and near its crossing with Chestnut Avenue and Park Avenue the drawing becomes dense, with a row of attached stores and dwellings, an auditorium, city stables, a Y.W.C.A. and a small triangle of lots between Morris Avenue and Cedar. St. Teresa's Roman Catholic church, rectory, convent and parochial school stand south of Morris Avenue, and the Fairview and Fair Oaks sanatoriums, both heated by steam and lit by electricity, lie on large grounds in the middle and lower left. The south half is residential: Prospect crosses the sheet from left to right, with Oakland Place and Linden Place below it, all with regular blocks of two-storey frame dwellings, a brook running down through the lots between Tulip and Larned Road. The west edge shows the Oakland and Linden lots of sheet 16. Water pipes of four to ten inches are drawn in the streets. The sheet is drawn at 100 feet to an inch.
notes: Junctions on Morris Avenue and George with Locust Drive disagreed with the rest of the fit by 5 to 14 m and were left out.
Tulip is Tulip Street, Maple is Maple Street and Prospect is Prospect Street in OpenStreetMap.
Park Avenue West is printed in brackets.
Hotel Suburban, the Fairview Sanatorium, the Fair Oaks Sanatorium and St. Teresa's Roman Catholic church and parochial school are named on the sheet.

100 ft. Springfield Av, Locust Dr, Morris Av, Park Av, Tulip, Prospect, Maple; Fair Oaks and Fairview sanatoriums. Morris Av and Cedar St left out (5-14 m off); north-east corner rests on extrapolation.

sheet-18.description: Sheet 18 covers the area of Summit between the Morris Avenue approach to the town centre and the residential district around Woodland Avenue. The Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad crosses the lower left diagonally, with Kent Place Boulevard running along its north side and Railroad Avenue on the south side, where a concrete bridge carries Springfield Avenue over the tracks. Norwood Avenue crosses the top left of the sheet and curves south as the main street through the middle, passing the grounds of Kent Place School, a large open campus with a gymnasium, a dormitory, class room buildings and a cafeteria, drawn with watchman, clock, steam heat and electric lights noted. East of Norwood Avenue the blocks between Sherman Avenue, Crescent Avenue, Hillside Avenue, De Forest Avenue and Woodland Avenue are filled with detached frame dwellings with garages, and Mac Gregor Road bounds the top. At the bottom of the sheet Springfield Avenue, Morris Avenue, Chestnut Avenue and Park Avenue enclose the edge of the business district, with a public school, a garage and auto repair shops, Fountain Baptist Church, shops and a hall. A large blue-coloured works stands beside the railroad west of Springfield Avenue. Four-inch to eight-inch water pipes and hydrants are drawn in most streets, and street widths of 40 and 50 feet are marked. Adjoining sheets are numbered 11, 12, 17, 19 and 2. The sheet is drawn at 100 feet to an inch.
notes: Mac Gregor Road is McGregor Road in OpenStreetMap, De Forest Avenue is Deforest Avenue, and the street printed Kent Place at the left edge is not in OpenStreetMap.
Railroad Avenue, along the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western tracks, is not in OpenStreetMap.
A concrete bridge carries Springfield Avenue over the railroad.
100 ft, rotation about +21. Kent Place School, D.L.&W. railroad, Springfield Av bridge.

sheet-19.description: Sheet 19 covers the Beechwood Road district of Summit, between Woodland Avenue on the west and Summit Avenue on the east, and from Badeau Avenue at the top to De Forest Avenue at the bottom. The north half is a residential area of detached frame dwellings with garages on regular lots, laid out around Beechwood Road, Shadyside Avenue and a loop formed by Hawthorne Place, with Bellevue running along the upper left and Badeau Avenue across the top. The east side along Summit Avenue is largely unbuilt lots, with a few houses and a large house with outbuildings near the top. Below Hawthorne Place the sheet carries the larger institutional buildings: the Beechwood Apartments west of Beechwood Road, two groups of apartment buildings and the Euclid Apartments beside Summit Avenue with blue tile partition buildings, and the Beechwood Hotel, a large brick-and-stone building with a ball room, standing in its own grounds between Euclid Avenue and De Forest Avenue. In the south-west corner the Calvary Episcopal Church, a parish house and Sunday school, and the Highland Club stand beside Larch Place. Turkey Hill Cottage and several stone houses stand on Euclid Avenue and Parmley Place. A garage and several houses line the north side of Euclid Avenue. Water pipes of four to eight inches and hydrants are drawn in the streets, and street widths of 40 and 50 feet are marked. Adjoining sheets are numbered 12, 13, 18, 2, 3, 20 and 37. The sheet is drawn at 100 feet to an inch.
notes: Mac Gregor Road is McGregor Road in OpenStreetMap, De Forest Avenue is Deforest Avenue, and Whittridge Road is Whittredge Road.
Highland Avenue is not in OpenStreetMap.
Beechwood Road meets Euclid Avenue in two places on the sheet, about 30 metres apart, as it does in OpenStreetMap.
Bellevue is printed without a suffix; it is Bellevue Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
100 ft. Beechwood Road district, Beechwood Hotel and apartments.

sheet-20-1.description: Sheet 20, part 1, covers a residential district in the north-east of Summit between Summit Avenue on the west and Hobart Avenue and Essex Road on the east, from Ridge Road at the top to Springfield Avenue at the bottom. Whittridge Road crosses the middle of the sheet, rising gently to the east, and the lettered street widths show it is 50 feet wide. North of Whittridge Road the blocks are large, with detached frame dwellings, many of them with garages, on deep lots between Summit Avenue, Fernwood Road and Hobart Avenue; two long blocks carry houses with a few larger estates, some drawn with a veneer covering, and the sheet numbers 60, 61 and 62 mark the lot groups. Hobart Road curves round the north-east corner, with Dogwood Drive branching from it. South of Whittridge Road, Waldron Avenue, De Barry Place and Hobart Avenue serve rows of narrow lots fully built with small frame houses, while the south-west corner next to Summit Avenue and Springfield Avenue is the most densely built part, with Parmley Court Apartments, the De Forest Apartments, a tile-partition apartment building, an auto repairing and furniture works, a hall and the Community Church. Euclid Avenue and Parmley Place join Summit Avenue on the west side. A fire alarm box stands on Whittridge Road near Waldron Avenue. Water pipes of four and six inches with hydrants are drawn in the streets. A heavy line cuts off the lower right, where a separate part continues the sheet (part 2). The sheet is drawn at 100 feet to an inch.
notes: De Barry Place is De Bary Place in OpenStreetMap, Whittridge Road is Whittredge Road, De Forest Avenue is Deforest Avenue, and Rutheven Place is Ruthven Place.
Hobart Road, with Dogwood Drive branching from it, borders sheet 37 on the north-east.
100 ft, two parts: main map and a small lower-right part (Whittridge Rd / Essex Rd) anchored on one hand-picked junction.

sheet-20-2.description: Sheet 20, part 2, is a small area in the lower right corner of the sheet, cut off from the main map by a heavy line that runs along its top and left sides. It shows the eastern end of Whittridge Road, drawn about 50 feet wide with a six-inch water pipe, and Essex Road running south-west from it. The only building is a single detached frame dwelling, lettered 73, standing on a lot between the two streets, and a small outbuilding stands on a narrow strip of ground beside the heavy line. The rest is open land laid out in lots. The part is the continuation of Whittridge Road and Essex Road beyond the edge of the main map, with the adjoining sheet numbers 37 above and 26 below. A hydrant stands on Essex Road. The part is drawn at the same 100 feet to an inch as the rest of the sheet, with its streets turned a few degrees from those of the main map.
notes: Whittridge Road is Whittredge Road in OpenStreetMap.
Placed from one hand-picked point at the Whittredge Road and Essex Road junction, with scale and rotation from the main part; low confidence.
100 ft, two parts: main map and a small lower-right part (Whittridge Rd / Essex Rd) anchored on one hand-picked junction.

sheet-21.description: Sheet 21 covers a large, mostly open tract in the south-west of Summit between Pine Grove Avenue on the west and Larned Road on the east, from Oak Knoll Drive at the top to Mountain Avenue near the bottom. Most of the ground is undeveloped and drawn as unbuilt blocks and lots; the streets are shown mainly as pairs of lines with a few buildings. Colony Drive, Monroe Avenue and the long curving Ashland Place are laid out across the middle of the sheet and marked 'not opened' in several places, and Ashland Place ends in a circular turning space lettered Colony Court. The only substantial institution is the International Sunshine Society's Arthur Home for Blind Babies, a group of frame buildings with steam heat, electric light, fire pails and extinguishers, standing on a large lot between Pine Grove Avenue and Colony Drive. A few frame dwellings and a greenhouse-like glass structure stand near Mountain Avenue, which crosses the lower part of the sheet from the lower left to Larned Road on the right and carries a 4-inch and 10-inch water main, and a junk store and a few houses lie along it. At the lower right Roosevelt Avenue and Magnolia Place leave Mountain Avenue. Colt Road enters Pine Grove Avenue at the left, and Grand Place and Olive Place run into Larned Road from sheet 22 at the right. The top of the sheet repeats the Oak Knoll Drive block of sheet 16. Adjoining sheet numbers 16, 22, 33, 34, 38, 120, 171, 328, 329 and 330 appear on the sheet. The scale is 100 feet to an inch.
notes: Pine Grove Avenue is Pinegrove Avenue and Ashland Place is Ashland Road in OpenStreetMap.

Colony Drive and Monroe Avenue are marked 'not opened' on the sheet; the junction of Colony Drive and Pinegrove Avenue in OpenStreetMap lies about 25 m from where the sheet draws it, so it was not used.
Oak Knoll Drive, Grand Place, Olive Place and Monroe Avenue are not in OpenStreetMap.
The International Sunshine Society's Arthur Home for Blind Babies stands between Pine Grove Avenue and Colony Drive.
100 ft. Sparse; Colony Dr and Monroe Av not opened. Low confidence.

sheet-22.description: Sheet 22 covers a residential district in the south-west of Summit, west of the Elm Street business area. It runs from Linden Place at the top to Mountain Avenue and Primrose Place at the bottom, and from Larned Road on the west to Elm Street on the east, with Oak Ridge Avenue crossing the lower right. The upper half is a regular grid of narrow house lots on Linden Place, Ashland Place, Tulip Street, Laurel Avenue and Maple Street, almost all two-storey frame dwellings with private garages behind. West of Tulip Street the block between Ashland Place, Larned Road and Myrtle Avenue is a park with a field house and a car shop, crossed by Park Way, and the Brayton School, a two-storey brick building with steam heat and electric light, stands beside it. Mountain Avenue cuts diagonally across the middle of the sheet towards Elm Place, lined with larger frame houses on deep lots. South of Myrtle Avenue the blocks between Larned Road and Tulip Street are cut by the short streets Grand Place and Olive Place into many small, mostly vacant lots. The south-east corner below Oak Ridge Avenue and Montview Road is undeveloped and shows only the number of the adjoining sheet, 38; Rowan Road leaves Oak Ridge Avenue there. Water pipes of six to ten inches are drawn in most streets, with hydrants marked. The sheet is drawn at 100 feet to an inch.
notes: Ashland Place is Ashland Road in OpenStreetMap.
Grand Place, Olive Place and Park Way are not in OpenStreetMap.
Brayton School stands west of Tulip Street beside the park.
100 ft. Pilot sheet. Linden Pl to Mountain Av, Larned Rd to Elm St; Brayton School.

sheet-23.description: Sheet 23 covers a residential district of central Summit south-west of the downtown blocks of sheets 2 and 3, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned about 64 degrees, so that north points towards the upper right. Morris Avenue crosses the sheet from the top to the bottom, with Cedar, Maple, Elm, Summit Avenue, Beauvoir Avenue and Sayre running off it. At the top are the Public Library and the Y.M.C.A. in block 114, with the Central Presbyterian Church and its Sunday school in block 115 below Maple; the Summit High School, a large brick building with a gymnasium and auditorium, stands in block 125 between Maple and Elm. East of Morris Avenue the block bounded by Elm, Summit Avenue and Park Avenue holds a playground and small houses, while a Gospel Hall and a block of stores lie at Summit Avenue and Walnut. West of Morris Avenue Elm Street runs diagonally to Elm Place, with Linden Place and Oakland Place laying out narrow house lots in block 128 and a greenhouse beside Sayre. The lower half is closely built with two-storey frame dwellings along William, Morris Avenue and Beauvoir Avenue, including a Swedish Lutheran church, while Mountain Avenue closes the sheet on the west and Sylvan Road curves at the lower right. Sheet numbers 17, 22, 27, 24, 5, 2 and 3 are printed in the margins for the adjoining sheets.
notes: Cedar is Cedar Street, Maple is Maple Street, Elm is Elm Street and William is William Street in OpenStreetMap.
Park Avenue is Broad Street in OpenStreetMap.
"Oakbidge Av." is printed at the foot of the sheet (checked at full resolution; probably a misprint); today's street at this place is Oakridge Avenue.
The sheet is turned about 64 degrees; the compass points to the upper right.
Morris Avenue and Sayre Street (12 m), Broad Street and Cedar Street (19 m) and Doremus Street and Elm Street (14 m) were rejected as outliers.
Morris Av district, 100 ft, turned about +64 degrees. High school, public library, Y.M.C.A.

sheet-24.description: Sheet 24 covers the north-west part of Summit between the Delaware, Lackawanna & Western Railroad and the Overlook Hospital grounds. The Lackawanna tracks cross the top of the sheet, with the Hill City Coal & Lumber Co. yard and its lumber sheds at the upper left and a small Central Atlantic States Service Corp. plant, with coal pockets and tanks, beside Park Avenue at the upper right. Scattered Lumber and Rahway Valley Railroad tracks curve down through the middle of the sheet. Park Avenue runs east to Ashwood Avenue, which follows the right edge of the sheet; Denman Place and Morris Avenue lead south and south-west from it. On the left, Walnut Street, Sylvan Road, Sylvan Terrace and Upper Overlook Road serve a district of small frame dwellings on narrow lots, while Lower Overlook Road and a loop of Upper Overlook Road enclose a hillside of larger houses. Overlook Hospital, with a Nurses Home and a 90 foot steel water tower, stands in the lower left, and a fire-proof wing built in 1927 is annotated on its front. At the bottom, Glenside Avenue, Baltusrol Road, Van Dyke Place, Henry Street and Pearl Street divide the south-east into blocks of frame dwellings and garages, with Russell Place and Michigan Avenue at the lower right edge. Mountain Avenue and Oak Ridge Avenue meet at the lower left. Water pipes of four to ten inches and hydrants are drawn in most streets. The adjoining sheets are numbered 5, 23, 25, 27, 28 and 29. The sheet is drawn at 100 feet to an inch.
notes: Sylvan Road, Sylvan Terrace, William Street and Ridgedale Place are not in the modern OpenStreetMap street data.
Oak Ridge Avenue is Oakridge Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
100 ft, rotation about -15. Overlook Hospital, Park Av and Morris Av district.

sheet-25-1.description: Part 1 of sheet 25 is the upper part of the sheet, lying north of the heavy line that follows the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad, in the north of Summit. Springfield Avenue crosses the top of the part, running from the upper left to the upper right, and Essex Road and Edgewood Road lead south from it. At the upper left is a small grid of narrow house lots on Rutheven Place, Hobart Avenue and Franklin Place, almost all two-storey frame dwellings with outbuildings, one of them outlined in blue and marked as a stone dwelling. Below Franklin Place a few more houses stand on long lots that run down toward the railroad, and a small group of pink and yellow buildings sits beside the railroad cut near the left edge. East of Hobart Avenue the district changes to large estates: a lane runs south-south-west between irregular lots numbered 317 and 133 and ends in a curved turn near the railroad, and Edgewood Road bends round a large oval enclosing block 135, with a handful of frame dwellings standing well apart in big grounds. Blocks 110, 133, 134, 135 and 136 are numbered. The right side of the part is mostly blank paper belonging to the neighbouring sheets 26 and 30, whose numbers are printed there. Water pipes of four, six and eight inches are drawn along Springfield Avenue, Hobart Avenue, Franklin Place and Edgewood Road. The compass, the oval Summit label and the sheet number are printed at the upper right. The part is drawn at 100 feet to an inch and its upper edge is cut off by sheet 20.
notes: Rutheven Place is Ruthven Place in OpenStreetMap; Debarry Place is De Bary Place; Lenox Avenue is Lenox Road.
The unnamed Lane south of Springfield Avenue is not in OpenStreetMap under a name; it runs between Hobart Avenue and Edgewood Road.
The Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad runs along the dividing heavy line between parts 1 and 2.
100 ft, two parts divided by the heavy line along the railroad: 1 upper (Springfield Av, Hobart Av, Edgewood Rd), 2 lower (Orchard, Park Av, Broad, Morris Av).

sheet-25-2.description: Part 2 of sheet 25 is the lower part of the sheet, south of the heavy line along the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad, and shows a compact residential district in the north-east of Summit. The railroad enters from the left as several tracks and swings across the upper left. Park Avenue and Orchard run north-east and south-west through the middle of the part, with Broad on the same trend to the east and Morris Avenue along the right edge; a short bent lane, Cottage Lane, links Orchard and Park Avenue. At the lower left Ashwood Avenue runs down the left edge to Park Avenue, and Orchard also turns east to meet it. Nearly all the lots carry two-storey frame dwellings with small outbuildings, but there is some denser building around Orchard and Park Avenue, with an auto repair building and a bakehouse. Public School No. 2, a large pink brick building lettered as heated by steam and lighted by electricity, with a fire alarm box in the building, stands at the lower left between Orchard and Park Avenue. Wallace Chapel, an African Methodist Episcopal Zion church, is drawn on the east side of Broad, and a storage warehouse stands on Broad near the bottom. Blocks 136, 155, 156 and 164 are numbered. Shunpike Road appears as a short stub at the bottom right. The north arrow at the lower right is turned well to the left of vertical. The part is drawn at 100 feet to an inch.
notes: Orchard is Orchard Street in OpenStreetMap; Broad is Broad Street.
The north arrow of this part is turned about 20 degrees to the left of straight up; the fit rotation is about -14 degrees.
The Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad is lettered D.L.&W.R.R. along the tracks at the left.
100 ft, two parts divided by the heavy line along the railroad: 1 upper (Springfield Av, Hobart Av, Edgewood Rd), 2 lower (Orchard, Park Av, Broad, Morris Av).

sheet-26.description: Sheet 26 shows a residential district in the north-west of Summit, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north points toward the upper left. Springfield Avenue runs along the bottom of the sheet. Essex Road forms the left boundary, curving down from the upper left to Springfield Avenue, and Whittridge Road enters at the upper left and runs north-east toward Westminster Road. Lenox Avenue runs through the middle of the sheet from the top down to Springfield Avenue, and a second street lettered Whittridge Road runs parallel to it on the east. Glendale Road comes in from the top right and joins Prospect Hill Avenue, which loops around the right side of the sheet and returns toward Springfield Avenue at the lower right. Edgewood Road leaves Springfield Avenue at the lower right. The blocks are cut into long irregular lots, many of them with a single two-storey frame dwelling and a garage; a few buildings are brick and a small building near the lower middle is marked fire proof construction. The lower right corner is more closely built with several houses on Prospect Hill Avenue and Springfield Avenue. Blocks 74 to 78 and 316 are numbered. A water main of six inches follows most of the streets. The compass is at the upper left and the oval Summit label at the upper right. Neighbouring sheets 20, 25, 30 and 37 are named in the margins.
notes: Whittridge Road is Whittredge Road in OpenStreetMap; Lenox Avenue is Lenox Road.
The fitted rotation is about -35 degrees; the compass north arrow points to the upper left, consistent with the fit.
Two streets are both lettered Whittridge Road, the diagonal road at the upper left and the central north-south one.
100 ft, turned about -35. Whittridge Rd, Lenox Av, Essex Rd, Prospect Hill Av.

sheet-27.description: Sheet 27 covers a residential district in the south-west of Summit, between Oak Ridge Avenue and Mountain Avenue at the top and Ridgedale Avenue at the bottom. The sheet is turned: the compass at the top shows north pointing towards the upper right, so the streets run at a steep slant across the page. Oak Ridge Avenue crosses the top left and curves down the middle of the sheet towards the lower right, with Elm and Mountain Avenue forming a triangle of blocks of small frame dwellings in the upper right, and Rowan Road curving across the middle left past a few larger houses on big lots, some of them brick or tile-roofed. Williams Street meets Mountain Avenue near the right edge. The central and lower part of the sheet is laid out around Glenside Avenue, which runs diagonally from the right edge towards the left, Baltusrol Place, which leaves it and runs down the left side, Hughes Place and Baltusrol Road. These streets enclose rows of narrow lots with frame dwellings and private garages, and a block of ruined or demolished buildings is marked near Hughes Place. Pearl Street and Van Dyke Place come in at the lower right, where a fire alarm box stands at the junction near the right edge; Ridgedale Avenue crosses the bottom. A long dashed strip at the left edge is lettered Proposed Street. The south-west corner is largely undeveloped and shows only the numbers of adjoining sheets 22, 23, 24, 28 and 38. Water pipes of four and six inches and hydrants are drawn in the streets. The sheet is drawn at 100 feet to an inch.
notes: Williams Street is William Street in OpenStreetMap.
Hughes Place was left out of the control: its modern junction with Baltusrol Road lies about 80 m from where the sheet draws it.
Proposed Street is not in the modern street data.
Oak Ridge Avenue appears as both Oak Ridge Avenue and Oakridge Avenue in OpenStreetMap.
100 ft, turned (north to upper right, rotation about +66). Oak Ridge, Mountain, Baltusrol and Glenside district. Hughes Place displaced (about 80 m), left out.

sheet-28.description: Sheet 28 covers the extreme south of Summit, where the city meets Springfield Township. Most of the sheet is open land. Built-up ground is confined to the upper left, where Pearl and Michigan Avenue run across the top and two short blocks of small frame dwellings and garages, with a few tile and concrete outbuildings, lie on either side of Ashwood Avenue between Pearl and the end of the lots. Ridgedale Avenue runs down the left side as a long narrow strip lined with a handful of houses near the top. Below the built-up part Ashwood Avenue and Ridgedale Avenue are laid out as 50 foot streets through undeveloped lots and farmland, and a dashed road winds across the open middle of the sheet. Baltusrol Road crosses the lower left on a long diagonal towards the south-east, with a small group of dwellings and a greenhouse range beside it, and Private Road branches off it near the foot of the sheet. A heavy dash-dot line running from the foot of the sheet to the upper right is the city limit; Springfield Township is lettered on its far side, and a margin note to the right directs the reader to the South Orange volume. The sheet is turned, with the compass at lower left showing north towards the upper left. Adjoining sheets 24, 27, 29 and 38 are named at the edges. The sheet is drawn at 100 feet to an inch.
notes: Along the Springfield Township line the sheet is marked 'City Limit'.
Margin note along the right side: 'See South Orange Volume' (read at overview resolution).
Private Road is probably the present Old Coach Road; this was not confirmed.
100 ft, mostly open land at the Springfield Township line, turned (rotation about -29); three control points.

sheet-29.description: Sheet 29 covers the southern edge of Summit's built-up area east of Ashwood Avenue, down to the Springfield Township line. The sheet is turned: the compass in the middle shows north towards the right, so Ashwood Avenue runs across the top and Morris Avenue down the right side. The built-up part occupies the upper half. In the upper left, between Pearl Street and Michigan Avenue, a small district of narrow lots with frame dwellings leads east along Russell Place past a fire alarm box, with two large greenhouse ranges and a block of open lots beside it. To the east, Russell Place and Morris Court serve blocks of two-storey frame dwellings with garages, and Oakes Memorial Church M.E. stands on the Ashwood Avenue side of the Russell Place blocks. Morris Avenue carries a trolley right of way along its east side, with shops, a dry cleaner and an auto repair garage near the top right where Park Avenue and Broad meet; the neighbouring sheet 25 is noted there. West of the houses the Stephens-Miller Co. building materials yard occupies a large tract served by railroad sidings, with warehouses, lumber piles and coal pockets, and the railroad tracks curve down the middle of the sheet. The lower two thirds is open land with a few scattered houses. A small stream runs across the bottom left beside the Springfield Township line, with a note to see the South Orange volume, and a small settlement along Shunpike Road, Yale Street and Princeton Street occupies the lower right corner, marked with sheet number 31. The sheet is drawn at 100 feet to an inch.
notes: Marginal note along the lower left: 'See South Orange Volume'.
The dash-dot line along the stream is lettered 'Springfield Township' and 'City Limit' (Springfield Township line).
Ashwood Avenue / Russell Place was rejected from the fit: the modern junction lies 12 m from the drawn one.
100 ft, turned (rotation about +77). Russell Place, Morris Court, Stephens-Miller yard, Springfield Township line.

sheet-30.description: Sheet 30 covers an area in the north-east of Summit, drawn at 100 feet to an inch, where the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad crosses the sheet diagonally from the lower left to the top as a bundle of parallel lines. West of the railroad, Prospect Hill Avenue curves along the upper left, with Argyle Court branching from it, and Springfield Avenue crosses the middle, running from the left edge across the railroad and then east to Clark Street. Large irregular lots, blocks 76, 78 and 337, are mostly empty with a few scattered dwellings. East of the railroad the built-up district centres on Park Avenue and Broad, which run north-east to south-west and are cut by the cross streets North, John, South and Orchard. Small frame dwellings fill the blocks, numbered 147, 149, 150, 151, 152, 153 and 154. Further north-east, Caldwell Avenue and Clark run between blocks 137 and 138 and 338, with houses lining Clark and a fire alarm box near Springfield Avenue. Chapel Street leaves Springfield Avenue at the right. Along the right edge a strip of the adjoining sheet 32 shows Chestnut Street, a lane and Summit Street. A dash and dot line lettered A to B runs across the top. The compass is at the upper left and the oval Summit label and sheet number at the upper right. Sheets 25, 26, 31, 32 and 37 are named in the margins.
notes: Clark is Clark Street, North is North Street, John is John Street, South is South Street, Orchard is Orchard Street and Broad is Broad Street in OpenStreetMap.
Argyle Court and the junction of Caldwell Avenue with Springfield Avenue are not on the modern lines; both were left out of the fit.
The Chestnut Street, Lane and Summit Street strip at the right edge repeats the edge of sheet 32.
100 ft, rotation about -16. Railroad diagonal; Park Av / Broad grid. Argyle Ct and Caldwell Av at Springfield Av displaced, left out.

sheet-31.description: Sheet 31 shows the north-east edge of Summit along Morris Avenue, drawn at 100 feet to an inch. Morris Avenue runs from the lower left up the left side of the sheet to Springfield Avenue and then north-east to the top right edge. At the upper left a small triangle of lots between Broad, Clark and Chapel lies north of Springfield Avenue, with a few frame dwellings. South of Springfield Avenue the built-up blocks between Broad and Morris Avenue, numbered 148, 150, 152 and 154, are cut by the cross streets North, John and South and carry rows of small dwellings; a filling station stands near Springfield Avenue. East of Morris Avenue the ground is mostly open: two long greenhouse ranges stand in the middle of the sheet, and a row of lots with dwellings faces Orchard, which runs straight east across the sheet. South of Orchard the streets Yale, Princeton and Harvard are lettered not opened and bound the blocks 165 to 168, one of which holds a further group of greenhouses. Shunpike Road crosses the bottom. A stream runs down the right side of the sheet along the Springfield Township city line, and a margin note reads See South Orange Volume. The compass is in the upper middle. Neighbouring sheets 25, 29, 30 and 32 are named in the margins.
notes: Chapel is Chapel Street in OpenStreetMap; North, John, South, Orchard and Broad are North Street, John Street, South Street, Orchard Street and Broad Street.
Yale, Princeton and Harvard are lettered not opened on the sheet.
100 ft, rotation about -26. Morris Av, Orchard; Yale/Princeton/Harvard not opened.

sheet-32.description: Sheet 32 covers the north-east corner of Summit, at the Springfield Township line, drawn at 100 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the left. The Morris and Essex Turnpike runs diagonally across the upper left, and the city line with Springfield Township follows the top edge, with a margin note reading See South Orange Volume. At the left, between Chestnut and the turnpike, the Public Service Gas Company has a works with a three million cubic foot gas holder, drawn as a large circle, and several brick buildings. The middle of the sheet is a wedge of streets: Broad runs from the upper left down the middle, Middle Avenue crosses it from the upper left to the lower right, Summit and Grove run to the south, and Washington Avenue and Grove join in a rounded turn near the bottom. Morris Avenue leaves the top and runs south-east along the right side, with Chapel at the bottom. Large greenhouse buildings are drawn in yellow at the top right, and a stream runs down the right side. The north-west and middle parts are mostly open lots, blocks 139 to 144, with a few dwellings; the main concentration of houses is east of Washington Avenue, block 146, and along Chapel. Some streets are lettered not opened. The compass at the lower right has its north arrow pointing left.
notes: The Morris and Essex Turnpike is now Route 24 with service roads, and was not used for control.
Broad is Broad Street, Grove is Grove Street and Chapel is Chapel Street in OpenStreetMap; Chestnut and Summit have no match in OpenStreetMap.
Fitted rotation is about -78 degrees, matching the compass; only four control points, two of them hand-picked.
100 ft, turned -78 (north to the left). Public Service Gas Co.; 4 points, 2 hand-picked.

sheet-33.description: Sheet 33 covers the south-western corner of Summit at 200 feet to an inch, an outlying district of woodland and large lots along the boundaries with Mountainside to the east and New Providence to the south. Mountain Avenue enters at the left edge and runs down the left side of the sheet, becoming a long, gently curved road that crosses the lower left past a small group of frame houses and a stream, with Division Avenue joining it near the bottom left. In the upper middle a planned subdivision, plotted into narrow lots laid out between Roosevelt Road, Oak Ridge Avenue and Greenbriar Drive, has a handful of frame dwellings and a round water tank with a main running to it, and Oak Ridge Avenue and Greenbriar Drive form a loop around the lots. Roosevelt Road enters from the upper left. Glenside Avenue crosses the right half of the sheet diagonally, and further right the Feltville Lake and its stream follow the Mountainside borough line, which is marked as a dash-dot line. The Sunnyside Fresh Air Camp for Children of the Newark Female Charitable Society, with a group of frame buildings, a boys' camp and a plant lodge, stands below the subdivision. Large parts of the sheet are blank with only property lines and block numbers. The south edge of the sheet follows the New Providence borough line. The compass is turned, with north pointing to the left.
notes: Placed from two junctions only (Greenbriar Drive / Oakridge Avenue at the top of the loop and Mountain Avenue / Pinegrove Avenue); position and scale come from those two points, so treat as low confidence.
Oak Ridge Avenue is Oakridge Avenue in OpenStreetMap; Pine Grove Avenue is Pinegrove Avenue.
Roosevelt Road is not in OpenStreetMap.
The Greenbriar Drive and Oak Ridge Avenue names change at the bottom of the loop, which is where OpenStreetMap has its second Greenbriar Drive / Oakridge Avenue node.
200 ft, north to the left. Oak Ridge Av / Greenbriar Dr, Sunnyside Fresh Air Camp, Feltville Lake; helmert from two junctions.

sheet-34.description: Sheet 34 covers the western edge of Summit at 200 feet to an inch, from Blackburn Road and Valley View Avenue at the top to Mountain Avenue near the bottom, and from the borough line along Division Avenue on the left to Pine Grove Avenue on the right. The upper left is a narrow strip of small frame houses between Division Avenue and Valley View Avenue, with a greenhouse at the left edge. Valley View Avenue runs east to meet Sunset Drive and continues as Blackburn Road along the top of the sheet. East of the large unplotted block in the middle, a grid of narrow lots has been laid out between Winchester Road, Warwick Road, Colt Road and Pine Grove Avenue, with the Franklin Public School, lit by electricity and heated by steam, on the block next to Blackburn Road and a Proposed Street cutting across the blocks. Lower down Colt Road, Pembrooke Road and Monroe Avenue are laid out but little built on, and Dr. Reinle's Sanitarium stands on a lot beside Pembrooke Road. In the lower right Valentine Hamann, florist, has long glasshouses beside Ashland Place, which meets Mountain Avenue. Mountain Avenue sweeps across the lower part of the sheet from Division Avenue at the lower left and carries a water main. Division Avenue carries a dash-dot city line. Most of the middle and lower sheet is blank, showing only lot lines and numbers belonging to adjoining sheets. Lettering that reads along the left edge, outside the drawn area, could not be read.
notes: Pine Grove Avenue is Pinegrove Avenue, Pembrooke Road is Pembroke Road and Ashland Place is Ashland Road in OpenStreetMap.
Proposed Street, Monroe Avenue and Colony Drive were not built as drawn.
The junction of Colt Road and Pembroke Road in OpenStreetMap near Winchester Road was rejected as 11.7 m off the fit; the Pembroke Road / Winchester Road node was kept with 5.5 m residual.
Franklin Public School, Dr. Reinle's Sanitarium and Valentine Hamann's greenhouses are named on the sheet.
200 ft. Blackburn Rd, Winchester/Warwick/Colt Rds, Pembrooke Rd.

sheet-35-1.description: The main part of Sheet 35 covers the north-western corner of Summit along the Passaic River, drawn at 200 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the left. Madison Avenue runs along the top with Lafayette Avenue and Evergreen Place leaving it, and Kent Place Boulevard comes down the right side to Passaic Avenue, which crosses the middle of the part towards the river. South of Passaic Avenue the boulevard continues as Mount Vernon Avenue, which crosses the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad and the Passaic River into the Township of Chatham, while New Providence Avenue, West End Avenue and Elkwood Place fan out to the east and Stanley Avenue runs along the river side of the railroad. Risk Avenue, marked not opened, runs along the right edge to the city line with the Borough of New Providence, where a brick incinerator stands. The railroad sweeps across the lower half in a wide curve. Most of the part is large open tracts with lot numbers; dwellings are scattered along Madison Avenue, Evergreen Place, Kent Place Boulevard and Passaic Avenue. The Summit Home for Children, with steam heat and electric light, stands in a large lot between Madison Avenue and Passaic Avenue. Across the river on the left is the Borough of Chatham, with a margin note to see the map of Chatham. A heavy line at the upper right cuts off a second part drawn on the same page.
notes: Mount Vernon Avenue south of Passaic Avenue is labelled "Mount Vernon Av. (Kent Place Blvd.)".
Elkwood Place is Elkwood Avenue in OpenStreetMap; Evergreen Place is not in OpenStreetMap.
Risk Avenue is marked "Not Opened".
The junction of Kent Place Boulevard, Mount Vernon Avenue and New Providence Avenue lies 11 m from the fit and was rejected; the modern junction has probably been rebuilt.
Lafayette Avenue / Madison Avenue was hand-picked.

200 ft, two parts, drawn with north to the left. Part 1 main map (Madison Av, Kent Place Blvd, Passaic Av to the Passaic River). Part 2 upper right: Passaic Av between Beekman Rd and Springfield Av, helmert on two junctions.

sheet-35-2.description: The second part of Sheet 35, cut off by a heavy line at the upper right of the page, shows a small area on the western edge of Summit by the Borough of New Providence, drawn at 200 feet to an inch with north to the left like the main part. Passaic Avenue runs across the top from Beekman Road to Springfield Avenue, which turns down the right edge to Division Avenue. The Passaic and Delaware branch of the Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad crosses the part diagonally, with the East Summit station at the bottom right. A few frame dwellings stand on the south side of Passaic Avenue, and an auto repair shop with gasoline tanks stands on Springfield Avenue. The rest of the part is open land in two large lots, crossed by Risk Avenue, marked not opened, and bounded below by the city line with the Borough of New Providence.
notes: "Divis Av." is Division Avenue (index and OpenStreetMap).
East Summit station ("E. Summit Sta.") of the Passaic and Delaware branch is drawn at the lower right.
Placed from two junctions only (helmert); low confidence.

200 ft, two parts, drawn with north to the left. Part 1 main map (Madison Av, Kent Place Blvd, Passaic Av to the Passaic River). Part 2 upper right: Passaic Av between Beekman Rd and Springfield Av, helmert on two junctions.

sheet-36.description: Sheet 36 covers the north-east corner of Summit along the Morris & Essex Turnpike and the Canoe Brook valley, at 200 feet to an inch. The turnpike crosses the top of the sheet, with a margin note directing the reader to the volume of South Orange; a poultry farm with a farmhouse, corn crib, ice house and poultry houses stands beside it at the upper right. Canoe Brook winds across the upper middle and through a pond at the upper left, and the long open tract between it and the Woodland Avenue line is lettered Canoe Brook Country Club. The only closely built district is at the left, along Canoe Brook Parkway and Wallace Road, where narrow lots on Rose Lane and the Parkway carry a thin scattering of dwellings, and a second group of small lots lies around Iris Road, Newton Avenue and Woodland Avenue in the middle left, near River Road, which runs down the left edge of the sheet. Woodland Avenue then runs south-east across the sheet as a long street with few buildings. In the lower left Greenfield Avenue, with a small row of dwellings, meets River Road beside a brook; below it Aubrey Street, Lafayette Avenue, Lewis Avenue, Sheridan Avenue and Beverly Road are laid out through open ground. At the right a few large houses stand on Bellevue Avenue, Hill Crest Avenue and a private road, Crest Acre Court, one house with a tile roof and fire-proof construction noted. Block numbers 301, 302 and 303 mark the subdivided tracts, and neighbouring sheets 6, 7, 8, 12, 13 and 37 are named at the edges. The sheet is turned about 25 degrees, with the compass in the upper left showing north towards the upper left.
notes: Margin note along the top: 'See Volume of South Orange'.

Hill Crest Avenue is Hillcrest Avenue and Bellevue Avenue is Bellevue Avenue in OpenStreetMap; Newton Avenue, Aubrey Street, Lewis Avenue, Sheridan Avenue and Crest Acre Court are not in the OpenStreetMap street data.
The modern Greenfield Avenue / River Road and Beverly Road / Woodland Avenue junctions lie about 30 m from where this sheet draws them, so they were not used for the fit.
200 ft, rotation about -24. Canoe Brook, Morris & Essex Turnpike; hand-picked control only (6 points over the upper left).

sheet-37-1.description: The main part of Sheet 37 covers the north-eastern residential hill district of Summit below the Morris and Essex Turnpike, which forms the city line with the area covered by the volume of South Orange along the top. It is drawn at 200 feet to an inch. Summit Avenue runs down the left side from the turnpike, with Bellevue Avenue to its west beside a brook, and Hill Crest Avenue, Lyric Lane, Edgemont Avenue and Badeau Avenue leaving it towards the south. In the middle Bow Lane, Fernwood Road and Brantwood Drive curve through large wooded estates, and Beacon Road joins Fernwood Road to Hobart Avenue, which climbs north-east to the turnpike. Ridge Road crosses the bottom of the part, and Hobart Road, Dogwood Drive and Whittridge Road run to Essex Road at the right edge. The lots are large and irregular, with scattered frame, brick and stone dwellings, several with private garages and one with a greenhouse; a gate house stands near the turnpike on Brantwood Drive, and a stone dwelling with a hollow-tile wall separating it from an auto house stands near Brantwood Drive. Lake View Avenue meets the turnpike at the bottom left near Badeau Avenue. A heavy line across the bottom of the page separates this part from a second part drawn below it, which continues the turnpike frontage further east.
notes: Margin note along the turnpike: "See Volume of South Orange"; the turnpike is marked as the city line.
Whittridge Road is Whittredge Road in OpenStreetMap; Hill Crest Avenue is Hillcrest Avenue.
Hobart Road south of Dogwood Drive is now part of Dogwood Drive.
The Morris and Essex Turnpike corridor is now Route 24 and its service roads; no turnpike junction was used.
Lyric Lane and Bow Lane are not in OpenStreetMap.
200 ft, two parts along the Morris & Essex Turnpike (city line). Part 1: Summit Av to Essex Rd. Part 2: Essex Rd to Middle Av, exact three-point fit.

sheet-37-2.description: The second part of Sheet 37, below the heavy line on the page, continues the strip of Summit south of the Morris and Essex Turnpike eastwards from Essex Road, drawn at 200 feet to an inch. The turnpike and the city line run along the top, with a margin note to see the volume of South Orange and South Terrace meeting the turnpike. Essex Road runs down the left edge, where Dogwood Drive and Whittridge Road leave it; Whittridge Road curves east to Lenox Avenue and Westminster Road, and Glendale Road runs down to Prospect Hill Avenue at the bottom. The Delaware, Lackawanna and Western Railroad crosses the turnpike and runs down the middle of the part in a cutting. On the right, Middle Avenue runs down the edge past the works of the Public Service Gas Company, with a note to see sheet 32 for detail, and Chestnut, marked not opened, and a lane cross the large tract numbered 336 below it. Most of this part is open land in large tracts; a handful of dwellings stand on Essex Road and Whittridge Road and a few small buildings and tanks stand by the turnpike.
notes: Placed from three detected junctions (Dogwood Drive / Essex Road, Essex Road / Whittredge Road, Westminster Road / Whittredge Road): an exact three-point fit whose scale and rotation agree with part 1. Lenox Road, Glendale Road and Prospect Hill Avenue junctions read on the sheet disagreed with the modern ones by 15 to 40 m and were not used. Low confidence on the right half.
Chestnut is marked "Not Opened".
Whittridge Road is Whittredge Road and Lenox Avenue is Lenox Road in OpenStreetMap.
200 ft, two parts along the Morris & Essex Turnpike (city line). Part 1: Summit Av to Essex Rd. Part 2: Essex Rd to Middle Av, exact three-point fit.

sheet-38-1.description: The main part of Sheet 38 covers the southern edge of Summit between Baltusrol Road and Mountain Avenue, drawn at 200 feet to an inch and turned so that north points to the left. Baltusrol Road runs along the top with Ashwood Avenue and a private road leaving it, and the line of Springfield Township runs down from it across the middle of the part; the Borough of Mountain Side lies along the right edge. Glenside Avenue crosses the part diagonally from upper left to lower right, with the Watchung Reservation riding stable beside it, and a private road leads from it to the Commonwealth Water Company's Baltusrol pumping station near a brook, with a note to see the enlarged plan on this sheet. A proposed street is drawn with dashed lines at the upper left. In the lower left, the only built-up area, Oak Ridge Avenue comes in from Rowan Road and Montview Road and runs down to Magnolia Place, Mountain Avenue and Roosevelt Road, with closely spaced frame and brick dwellings, a reservoir, a stand pipe and a junk yard at the corner of Mountain Avenue. Primrose Place leaves Oak Ridge Avenue near the top of that area. The rest of the part is open land in large numbered tracts. A heavy box at the right edge holds an inset of the pumping station drawn at 50 feet to an inch.
notes: The private road leaving Baltusrol Road at the top is today's Old Coach Road (junction with Baltusrol Road and Ascot Way).
Roosevelt Road is not in OpenStreetMap under that name.
Glenside Avenue south-west of Baltusrol Road was largely rebuilt with Interstate 78; no Glenside Avenue junction was used.

200 ft, drawn with north to the left. Part 1 main map (Baltusrol Rd, Glenside Av, Oak Ridge Av). Part 2: inset of the Commonwealth Water Co. Baltusrol pumping station at 50 ft, placed from two building corners carried from part 1.

sheet-38-2.description: This inset on Sheet 38, enclosed by a heavy line at the right of the page and drawn at 50 feet to an inch with north to the left, shows the Commonwealth Water Company's Baltusrol pumping station in the lot numbered 224, with a note "For Location See This Sheet" referring to its position on the main map. The station is a fireproof brick building of 1916 with concrete floors and roof, with boiler and engine rooms; a man is always on duty, it is heated by steam, lit and powered by electricity and fired by coal, and fire pails and extinguishers are provided. Twelve and ten inch water pipes run from it, and a hydrant with 100 feet of hose stands beside it. A small oil house, a storage shed and a tile structure stand nearby. A brook runs down the left side of the inset.
notes: Placed from two corners of the station building carried from the main part (sheet-38-1) at 50 feet to an inch (7.96 px/ft) with north set to -83 degrees, the main part's fitted rotation; the second corner lies 0.9 m from the anchored fit. Low confidence.

200 ft, drawn with north to the left. Part 1 main map (Baltusrol Rd, Glenside Av, Oak Ridge Av). Part 2: inset of the Commonwealth Water Co. Baltusrol pumping station at 50 ft, placed from two building corners carried from part 1.
